study.sample: 48participants,73%women,mean age20.42; paired robot-versus-cube comparison. Reported t47 and F2,94 agree with48complete paired cases. Registration targets45required and about50recruits, with technical/instruction/missing-data exclusions. Actual recruitment/exclusion flow not supplied and not reconstructed.
study.sequence: Five minutes of quarter-turn peg work, then Quick-Tap against an emotion-simulating Cozmo, then pickup familiarization and robot/cube shaking in counterbalanced order. The robot displays distress during/after shaking; cube does not. Prior game, object category, appearance, responsiveness and social interaction are not independently separated.
study.shaking: Paper says two shake trials of5and8seconds per target; frozen procedure says6and10seconds, different hands and a10-second break. The protocol difference needs clarification rather than an invented corrected duration.
study.measures: Current-state boredom/guilt among short PANAS items on1–5; agency/experience statements on1–7; paper reports19items(7agency/12experience), while frozen Measures describes17total and placeholder reliabilities. No final item list or alpha estimates independently verified.
study.allocation: Participants are told they face180seconds additional peg-turning and can exchange one second of robot/cube shaking for six seconds saved, choosing0–30seconds. Less chosen robot shaking is scored as more altruistic. Choice difficulty and response time measured. Frozen procedure explicitly says participants are ultimately told they need not repeat peg-turning.
study.boredom: Peg task produces more boredom than both shaking tasks, repeated F2,94=50.08,p<.001,partialeta.516; Bonferroni comparisons. Unpleasantness differences nonsignificant. Boredom, unpleasantness and resource cost are not interchangeable.
study.guilt_mind: After shaking:robot guilt2.42versuscube1.10,t47=6.634,p<.001,dz.957;agency3.07versus1.14,t47=8.975;experience2.68versus1.125,t47=8.062. These are felt/attributed human responses, not observed robot pain.
study.choice_results: Cube30-secondchoice33people,zero7;robot30-secondchoice16,zero15. Mean chosen shaking23.65seconds cube versus14.625robot;paired t47=−4.114,p<.001,dz−.594. Source reports Wilcoxon check agrees. Decision difficulty higher for robot; decision-time difference43.69versus35.86seconds is nonsignificant,p=.153.
study.regression: Exploratory model of robot shaking choice with guilt, agency and experience:F3,44=4.189,p<.05;guilt B−2.855,SE1.312,p<.05. Adding fear of breakage and prior Cozmo experience yields R²change.004,p=.896;guilt remains nominally significant,B−3.175,SE1.508. Other predictors are nonsignificant, not proved irrelevant or weaker than guilt by a coefficient-comparison test.
study.preregistration: Registration lists the three paired robot/object hypotheses and mentions regression inq22; the paper labels regression exploratory and explicitly acknowledges insufficient power for predictor analysis. Preplanned exploratory analysis is not a contradiction or evidence of hidden posthoc invention.
study.next_steps: Planned emotion-versus-no-emotion follow-up n140is not completed data in this four-page pilot. Public later Study2 materials/data cannot be counted as this paper’s additional participants or an independently read follow-up publication.
study.scope: The source itself acknowledges that robot-versus-object comparison cannot isolate simulated emotion. Guilt is measured rather than randomized. Actual benefits to the robot, realized costly helping, unique altruistic motive and machine subjective experience are not established.

summary: Add Altruistic behavior as a broad benefit-at-personal-cost construct, explicitly distinguishing it from harm aversion, cost sensitivity and selfless motive. This pilot measures anticipated-cost choices, not verified completed costly helping. Enrich existing guilt and capacity-attribution entries; preserve declared exploratory limits and source protocol discrepancies.

findings.definition: Behavior that benefits another party at a personal cost to the actor.
findings.origin: Social psychology / behavioral economics / costly helping
findings.novelty_rationale: A broad outcome-and-cost definition differs from reluctance to cause harm, which need not incur a cost, and cost sensitivity, which describes how helping changes as cost varies. Active resource-giving can satisfy this definition without a threat of inflicted harm. This pilot’s protection choice overlaps harm aversion operationally; the added family is not a claim of an independent mechanism or an additional distinct observed event.

evidence.quote: benefits others at a personal cost

findings.evidence_scope: Explicit behavioral definition. The pilot records choices to accept anticipated peg-turning time rather than shake a robot; initial interactions are real, while final additional cost is not verified as incurred and the registered procedure waives the repeat task. Treat this as an operational willingness measure, not proof of completed costly altruistic action.
findings.boundary: Behavioral altruism does not establish a consciously selfless motive, subjective machine concern, actual recipient suffering or an ethically optimal choice. Verify a genuine benefit and actual cost; guilt relief, attachment, demand and ordinary object preservation can also explain choices. Legitimate budgets, safety, rights, fairness and consent still constrain helping.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Explicit human behavioral construct; pilot uses anticipated-cost protection choices, and an agent analogy remains untested
findings.ai_proposal: Within an authorized budget, distinguish stated willingness to help from executed assistance that yields a verified benefit while imposing a recorded time/resource cost on the helper. For agents, describe observed allocation rather than felt selflessness; record who actually bears system costs and retain privacy, safety and stop constraints.

findings.definition: Remorse or self-blame about a perceived moral failure, often accompanied by a wish to repair harm.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing guilt, harm-avoidance and capacity-attribution records with a live-interaction pilot; preserve its prospective-choice and exploratory-association limits rather than add a synonymous mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: A current-state guilt item after real robot/object shaking is higher for the robot and negatively associated with chosen future robot-shaking time in a declared exploratory regression. The paper acknowledges that the regression is underpowered.
findings.boundary: Retrospective guilt is distinct from anticipated guilt, legal culpability or AI remorse. Association does not establish guilt as the unique causal driver, a mediator or stronger than nonsignificant capacity coefficients. Simulated distress, prior interaction, attachment and demand remain alternatives.

findings.definition: Reluctance to inflict harm, reflected in how strongly prospective harm is weighed against benefits when choosing an action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing guilt, harm-avoidance and capacity-attribution records with a live-interaction pilot; preserve its prospective-choice and exploratory-association limits rather than add a synonymous mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Participants choose less additional robot shaking than cube shaking when shaking saves anticipated boring work. The source labels costly protection altruistic; this observable contrast overlaps harm avoidance and includes a stated time tradeoff.
findings.boundary: No subjective robot harm, actual damage, universal rights, completed additional effort or fitted harm-utility parameter is established. Distress display and target kind are confounded. Initial shaking occurs, but the later cost choice is not verified as implemented.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing guilt, harm-avoidance and capacity-attribution records with a live-interaction pilot; preserve its prospective-choice and exploratory-association limits rather than add a synonymous mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Agency and experience ratings are collected after real shaking; both are higher for Cozmo than its nonresponsive cube. Paper reports19items versus17in the frozen measurement plan; the implemented final item set is unresolved.
findings.boundary: Attribution is not real mental capacity. A robot/object comparison after a social game does not isolate emotion simulation, validate universal dimensionality or prove that all cost-protecting behavior arises from perceived mind.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing guilt, harm-avoidance and capacity-attribution records with a live-interaction pilot; preserve its prospective-choice and exploratory-association limits rather than add a synonymous mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Reported seven-item agency ratings are higher for the robot. Agency does not independently predict chosen shaking time in the small exploratory joint model.
findings.boundary: A nonsignificant adjusted coefficient is not proof of zero influence or equivalence. Predictor overlap, sample size and measurement adaptations limit inference; perceived independent action is not genuine moral agency or a model’s felt autonomy.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing guilt, harm-avoidance and capacity-attribution records with a live-interaction pilot; preserve its prospective-choice and exploratory-association limits rather than add a synonymous mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Paper reports a twelve-item experience score higher for the robot than cube. It does not independently predict chosen shaking time in the exploratory joint model.
findings.boundary: Felt experience is attributed by humans, not verified in the robot. The frozen plan states17total items instead of the paper’s19; do not invent a corrected item count or reduce it automatically to another study’s canonical scale.

findings.definition: The extent to which helping changes as the helper's own costs increase or personal instrumental benefits decrease.
findings.novelty_rationale: Enrich existing guilt, harm-avoidance and capacity-attribution records with a live-interaction pilot; preserve its prospective-choice and exploratory-association limits rather than add a synonymous mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The task offers one fixed exchange rate between additional work and shaking time, permitting an anticipated-cost allocation choice. It provides context for helping costs rather than an independent manipulation of marginal cost.
findings.boundary: Boundary-only measurement lead. No varying-price experiment, verified realized cost curve or uniquely altruistic objective is shown. The new altruistic-behavior family concerns benefit at a cost; cost sensitivity concerns response to cost changes.

Preserve both version-specific descriptions instead of inventing the actual duration or alleging concealment.

Frozen Measures describes17capacities and placeholder alpha values; paper states19items,7agency/12experience. These differ from one another, but no implemented questionnaire/code/item-level dataset was read. Do not automatically force another study’s item count or present placeholders as published reliability results.

The paper elicits choices about repeating peg-turning; frozen procedure ends by waiving that repeat task. The paper does not document execution of selected additional time. Interpret willingness under anticipated cost separately from observed completed costly helping; exact implemented debrief/final-task history remains unverified.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The public registrationq22explicitly mentions the guilt/mind regression, and the paper labels it exploratory and underpowered. Preplanning does not make every estimate confirmatory, but exploratory labeling does not establish undeclared HARKing.
n=xxandalpha=.xxin frozen attachments are planned-report templates from before data collection, not published numerical results or evidence that the completed pilot data were fabricated.
The identifier is a registration, not a standard project node. Public registration API and archived files resolve, so the initial node404 is not evidence of a nonexistent preregistration.

Questionnaire header explicitly identifies Study2with emotion/no-emotion conditions. It is not automatically the pilot’s final questionnaire, and planned140participants are not counted as pilot observations.

methodological_limits: Small within-subject pilot and limited recruitment population. Paired comparisons and Bonferroni task contrasts are appropriate to the stated design; this does not establish broad generalization.
Real initial interaction must be distinguished from the final prospective cost choice. The registered plan waives repeating peg-turning; realized costly helping is not documented.

Emotion-simulating robot differs from cube in embodiment, responsiveness, prior game relationship and possible damage concerns. The paper explicitly says this contrast cannot isolate emotion simulation.

Current guilt is measured after shaking, not randomized independently. The declared exploratory regression cannot identify unique mediation, necessity, motive or superiority over nonsignificant predictors.
Perceived agency/experience do not prove actual sentience, pain or moral status. Avoid assuming that every protected object is a moral patient or that every helping choice is objectively beneficial.

One cost exchange rate and single prospective allocation do not establish a full cost-response function. Costly protection overlaps harm aversion; it is not another proven independent basic mechanism.

Registered17versusreported19items and shake timing differences require version/implementation clarification. Counterbalancing addresses order on average without guaranteeing absence of all carryover/demand effects.

Registration timestamp and frozen attachment hashes verified, but data-creation date is self-declared and actual adherence/exclusions are not reconstructed. Raw data not read; later Study2 files excluded from pilot evidence.

cross_paper_learning.finding: That later same-author vignette work measures perceived prosociality of a fictional human actor, not actual prosocial conduct. Here a live-interaction pilot explicitly defines costly altruistic behavior but measures anticipated-cost choices. Do not collapse the distinct outcome types or call one an independent replication of the other.
Use the existing harm-aversion/experience constructs while retaining subjective attribution versus actual machine suffering and parameter-estimation limits.
Existing cost-sensitivity-in-helping concerns how helping varies with cost, while altruistic behavior is the broader benefit-at-cost family. Related descriptions do not prove separate mechanisms.
Retrospective guilt, anticipated guilt, intention and actual completed action require distinct evidence. Do not inherit a broad abstract behavior claim without inspecting procedure and measures.
Real paid redistribution choices and this pilot’s waived anticipated work costs have different incentive depth; do not describe both as equally verified completed costly action.

deferred.term: Guilt-driven altruism as a newly proved mechanism
deferred.reason: Guilt is an exploratory measured correlate, not independently manipulated or established as a unique cause. Enrich existing Guilt instead of coining a new driver.

deferred.term: Boredom and emotion-simulation as additional extracted mechanisms
deferred.reason: Boredom is a task manipulation check and simulated emotion is confounded with target type; this paper does not independently define/test each as a new AI mechanism.

deferred.term: Completed emotion-versus-no-emotion effect from planned n140
deferred.reason: Future experiment described as next step; later materials/data are outside this pilot’s reported findings and have not been fully read as a separate paper.

limitations: One broad behavioral family added with explicit overlap and anticipated-cost boundaries; six existing records enriched. Eleven categories, stable IDs and unnumbered rows retained. No new ethical principle, subjective AI altruism, source quota, invented annual count, automatic harm edge, full-paper Markdown copy or independent replication claim.
